import os
import subprocess
import sys

from sase.vcs_provider import get_vcs_provider

checkout_target = {{ setup.checkout_target | tojson }}
project_name = {{ setup.project_name | tojson }}
gh_ref = {{ gh_ref | tojson }}

provider = get_vcs_provider(os.getcwd())

# Checkout the PR branch so that subsequent diffs are relative to the
# PR tip rather than the default branch. Try checkout_target first
# (works for default-branch refs like origin/main), then fall back to
# Patch name -> branch name conversion.
is_patch = checkout_target == f"origin/{gh_ref}"
ok, err = provider.checkout(checkout_target, os.getcwd())
if not ok:
    if is_patch:
        # Patch ref — resolve name to branch name
        resolved = provider.resolve_revision(
            gh_ref, project_name, os.getcwd()
        )
        ok, err = provider.checkout(resolved, os.getcwd())
    else:
        # Project/repo ref — try common default branch names
        for fallback in ["master", "main"]:
            ok, err = provider.checkout(fallback, os.getcwd())
            if ok:
                break
    if not ok:
        print(
            f"Warning: checkout failed: {err}",
            file=sys.stderr,
        )

# Sync with remote after checkout
subprocess.run(
    ["git", "pull", "--rebase", "--quiet"],
    capture_output=True,
    text=True,
    check=False,
)

# Record HEAD for the diff step
result = subprocess.run(
    ["git", "rev-parse", "HEAD"],
    capture_output=True,
    text=True,
    check=False,
)
head = result.stdout.strip() if result.returncode == 0 else ""
print(f"head_before={head}")
print("success=true")

head_before="{{ checkout.head_before }}"
if [ -z "$head_before" ]; then
  exit 0
fi
head_now=$(git rev-parse HEAD)
diff_dir="${SASE_TMPDIR:-${SASE_HOME:-$HOME/.sase}/tmp}/gh-diffs"
mkdir -p "$diff_dir"
diff_file=$(mktemp "$diff_dir/sase-gh-XXXXXX.diff")
if [ "$head_now" != "$head_before" ]; then
  # Commits were made — show only the last commit's diff
  git diff HEAD~1 HEAD > "$diff_file" 2>/dev/null
  commit_msg=$(git log -1 --format='%s' HEAD)
  echo "meta_commit_message=$commit_msg"
else
  # No commits — show uncommitted changes
  git diff HEAD > "$diff_file" 2>/dev/null
  git ls-files --others --exclude-standard -z 2>/dev/null \
    | while IFS= read -r -d '' f; do
        git diff --no-index /dev/null "$f" 2>/dev/null
      done >> "$diff_file"
fi
if [ -s "$diff_file" ]; then
  echo "diff_path=$diff_file"
else
  rm -f "$diff_file"
fi

# Stash any uncommitted changes (including untracked files)
if ! git diff --quiet HEAD 2>/dev/null || [ -n "$(git ls-files --others --exclude-standard)" ]; then
  git stash push --include-untracked -m "gh-workflow-$(date +%s)" --quiet
  echo "stashed=true"
else
  echo "stashed=false"
fi
git fetch origin --quiet 2>&1 || true
git pull --rebase --quiet 2>/dev/null || true
echo "success=true"

from sase_github.scripts.gh_setup import main
main(
    gh_ref={{ gh_ref | tojson }},
    n={{ n | tojson }},
    release={{ release | tojson }},
    workflow_label={{ workflow_label | tojson }},
)

However, an analysis of the production draft created today in [`2026-W45.md`](file:///home/bryan/bob/2026/2026-W45.md#L33-L78) reveals that the `v1` prompt contract produces low-signal, mechanical output: - **Redundancy:** Top tasks are duplicated between "Where the time went" and "Finished", burning ~25% of the 250-word cap. - **Routine Chore Spam:** 5 of the 7 slots in "Finished" were consumed by routine daily review rows (`[[gtd_daily]]`), obscuring actual project deliverables. - **Number Regurgitation:** The `**Headline:**` repeats total hours and percentage deltas already shown in the stats strip above `## Review` and in parent tables. - **Ignored Qualitative Context:** `bob periods brief` already extracts Bryan's manual log entries ("Bryan's words"), work-type distribution (BUILD vs. PLAN vs. FIX), and off-clock personal areas (Abby, Kelly, Body), but `v1` instructions never tell agents to use them. - **Nagging Auditing Questions:** Questions focus on checklist compliance (e.g. asking why Wednesday missed closeout) rather than strategic GTD reflection. --- ### 2. Recommended Changes: The `weekly v2` Prompt Contract Updating `src/native/periods/instructions.rs` to **`weekly v2`** (and rolling it out across the vault via `bob periods ensure -R`) introduces five high-impact refinements: 1. **Narrative Headline without Metric Repetition:** Summarize the week's defining accomplishment or strategic focus without reciting total hours or deltas already rendered in the stats strip. 2. **Deduplicated & Filtered "Finished" Section:** Exclude tasks already highlighted in "Where the time went"; filter out recurring checklist chores (`[[gtd_daily]]`, routines, pills); and compact routine completions into a single phrase (e.g. *"Daily review closed 6/7 days"*), freeing up slots for actual shipped deliverables. 3. **Incorporate Work Types & Off-Clock Balance:** Synthesize the balance of work types (e.g. BUILD 43%, PLAN 30%, FIX 17%) and off-clock personal areas (e.g. 11h 30m across Abby, Kelly, Body) to give visibility into cognitive labor and life balance. 4. **Leverage "Bryan's Words":** Instruct agents to consult the `## Bryan's words` section of `bob periods brief` to ground the narrative in Bryan's stated intentions, epic launches, and context. 5. **Re-orient "Questions" Toward Strategic GTD Decisions:** Frame questions around trade-offs, next steps on shipped work, and pruning vs. scheduling decisions for chronic rotten keeps (3+ keeps), rather than administrative compliance audits. --- ### 3.
